source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.1.2 List Properties (PDF 92-93, printed 89-90). The printed list omits a comma ('"Plates" "Balloons"'), and 'Homogeneous vs. Heterogeneous' code prints '3. 14'; a cleaned version is carried. Long question 1 is answered.

items: Dynamic size: a list can grow or shrink as items are added or removed.
Index-based access: the first item has index 0, the second 1, and so on.
Ordered collection: items keep the order in which they were added.
Heterogeneous elements: one list can hold numbers, words and even other lists.
Mutability: items can be updated, added or removed after creation.
Supports duplicates: the same value can appear more than once.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
items = ["Decorations", "Snacks", "Cold drinks", "Plates", "Balloons"]
items.append("Party Hats")
items.remove("Snacks")
print("After modifications:", items)
print("Heterogeneous list:", ["Apple", 42, 3.14, True])
print("Number of items:", len(items))    # 5
print("Item at index 2:", items[2])      # Plates

After the changes the list is Decorations, Cold drinks, Plates, Balloons, Party Hats: the order is kept and the list grew and shrank as needed. Lists can be nested, lists inside lists, which is useful for complex data (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Discuss the dynamic size property of lists and how it makes them flexible (long question 1).
blocks.explanation: A Python list does not need its size fixed in advance: append(), insert() and extend() make it grow and remove(), pop() and clear() make it shrink, and Python adjusts the memory automatically. So a program can store data whose amount is unknown, such as user input, shopping-cart items or tasks, without wasting space or running out of room.

items: List properties: dynamic size, index from 0, ordered, mixed types, mutable, duplicates allowed.
